verses.text: Jesus looked up and saw rich people putting their gifts into the temple offering box.
He also saw a poor widow put in two small brass coins.
He said, "I tell you the truth, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.
They all gave gifts out of what they had to spare. But she, out of her poverty, put in all she had to live on."
Some of his followers were talking about the temple, how it was decorated with beautiful stones and gifts offered to God. Jesus said,
"As for what you see here, the days will come when not one stone will be left on another. Every one of them will be thrown down."
They asked him, "Teacher, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign that they are about to take place?"
He replied, "Watch out that you are not led astray. Many will come in my name, saying, 'I am he,' and, 'The time is near.' Do not follow them.
When you hear of wars and riots, do not be terrified. These things must happen first, but the end will not come at once."
Then he said, "Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes, famines, and plagues in many places. There will be fearful events and great signs from heaven.
But before all this, people will arrest you and persecute you. They will hand you over to synagogues and prisons, and bring you before kings and governors because of my name.
This will be your chance to speak for me.
So make up your minds not to worry beforehand about how you will defend yourselves.
I will give you words and wisdom that none of your enemies will be able to resist or contradict.
You will even be handed over by parents, brothers, relatives, and friends, and they will put some of you to death.
Everyone will hate you because of my name.
But not a hair of your head will be lost.
By standing firm you will gain your lives.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its destruction is near.
Then those in Judea must run to the mountains. Those inside the city must leave. Those in the country must not enter the city.
These are days of punishment, so that everything that is written will come true.
How terrible for women who are pregnant and for those nursing babies in those days! There will be great distress in the land and anger against this people.
They will fall by the sword and be taken as prisoners to all the nations. Jerusalem will be trampled by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles are finished.
There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars. On the earth, nations will be in anguish and confusion at the roaring of the sea and the waves.
People will faint from fear and from dread of what is coming on the world, because the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
When these things begin to happen, stand up and lift your heads, because the time when you will be set free is near."
Then he told them this story. "Look at the fig tree, and all the trees.
When they sprout leaves, you see for yourselves and know that summer is near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God is near.
I tell you for certain, the people of today will not pass away until all these things have happened.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will never pass away.
Be careful, or your hearts will be weighed down with wild living, drunkenness, and the worries of life, and that day will close on you suddenly like a trap.
It will come on everyone who lives on the face of the whole earth.
So stay awake at all times, and pray that you may be counted worthy to escape all that is about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man."
Each day Jesus taught in the temple, and each evening he went out and spent the night on the hill called Olivet.
And all the people came early in the morning to the temple to hear him.
